baseline.disclaimer: This is an independent conceptual study and is not an official ESO instrument model.
baseline.validation: Synthetic only; no OOPAO or observational validation

conclusions: At zero jitter, increasing residual WFE from 0 to 500 nm changes mean SMF coupling from 0.699 to 0.020; wavefront quality sets the photon budget.
At 150 nm WFE, increasing per-axis jitter from 0 to 40 mas changes SMF coupling from 0.489 to 0.249; injection stability remains important even at fixed AO residual.

At 400 nm WFE / 10 mas jitter, replacing the SMF with a 15-port lantern changes forecast σRV from 12.98 to 8.75 m/s at baseline brightness, but from 403.84 to 502.86 m/s at 1/100 brightness. Under the assumed insertion loss and extraction noise, detector costs can reverse the throughput advantage.
